conventions.convention: The continuum torus is (R/Z)^d with product Haar measure of total mass one; e_k(x) = exp(2πi k·x), Fourier coefficients use e_{−k}, and Δ = Σ_i ∂²_{x_i}. Weak solutions are families of real L∞ classes with continuous smooth-test pairings satisfying the integral heat identity.

N ≥ 3; nearest-neighbor bonds are unordered and counted once. Each occupation-changing bond swap has rate N². Coordinates and diffusive time are dimensionless, with continuum diffusion coefficient D = 1.

Generators act on column observables and row probabilities satisfy p′ = pL. The full process permits arbitrary initial laws and is reducible across particle-number sectors; empty and full sectors are singleton constant chains.
The empirical measure is N^(−d) Σ_x η_x δ_{x/N}, a positive measure of mass at most one, rather than necessarily a probability measure.
The bracket convention is a continuous predictable increasing compensator A starting at zero such that M² − A is a martingale.
The heat-flow construction assumes Countable Choice; the stochastic realization, martingale results and hydrodynamic theorem assume full Choice.

Convergence is in probability against each fixed real smooth periodic test, uniformly over each fixed finite time interval. Probability spaces may vary with N; no common coupling or empirical measurement is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, for measurable 0 ≤ ρ₀ ≤ 1 on the normalized torus, the Fourier multiplier exp(−4π²|k|²t) constructs the unique weak heat solution. It is smooth for positive time, preserves bounds and mass, and satisfies ∫ρ_t G = ∫ρ₀ P_t G. For smooth periodic G, P_t G is smooth through t = 0 with uniformly bounded derivatives on compact time intervals.

Assuming Choice, SSEP on (Z/NZ)^d, N ≥ 3, is the uniformized finite-state chain whose occupation-changing unordered nearest-neighbor swaps have rate N². Its empirical measure is N^(−d) Σ_x η_x δ_{x/N}, and Δ_N is N² times the sum of coordinate centered second differences.

Assuming Choice, for the defined SSEP and a real smooth time-dependent periodic test H on [0,T] × T^d, the empirical pairing minus its initial value and the integral of the pairing with ∂_s H + Δ_N H is a square-integrable martingale. Its compensated squared-jump process is continuous, predictable and increasing, with terminal bound T N^(−d) Σ_i sup_s ‖∂_i H(s,·)‖∞².

Assuming Choice, for SSEP with any initial probability vector and a real smooth periodic G, M_t = ⟨π_t^N,G⟩ − ⟨π_0^N,G⟩ − ∫₀ᵗ⟨π_s^N,Δ_N G⟩ ds is a square-integrable martingale. Its bracket is the integral of the bond rates times squared empirical jumps, and A_T ≤ T N^(−d) Σ_i ‖∂_i G‖∞².

Assuming Choice, fix d ≥ 1 and finite T ≥ 0. If the initial SSEP empirical measures converge in probability against every real smooth periodic test to ρ₀ dx, with measurable ρ₀ taking values in [0,1], then for every such test G and every ε > 0, P_N(sup_{0≤t≤T}|⟨π_t^N,G⟩ − ∫ρ_t G dx| > ε) → 0, where ρ_t is the unique weak heat solution.

For every finite connected simple undirected graph G with m ≥ 1 vertices and every integer 0 ≤ k ≤ m, the graph of k-element vertex subsets connected by moving one occupied vertex along an edge to a vacant vertex is connected.

published_dependencies.used_for: The full Choice assumption carried by finite stochastic constructions and their consumers.
The weaker choice assumption stated for weak heat solutions and Fourier heat flow.
Normalized torus characters, Fourier signs, coefficients and trigonometric polynomials.
Fourier completeness, Parseval, identification of smooth Fourier sums, L² continuity at zero and uniqueness of weak heat solutions.
The irreducible reversible-model interpretation of nontrivial fixed-occupancy sectors, with zero energies and uniform stationary weights; not used to define the reducible full SSEP.
Predictable sigma-algebra conventions and predictability of continuous adapted bracket processes by left-step approximation, without completing or right-continuizing the filtration.

seams_checked.note: Checked the finite-generator definition, uniformization existence proof, finite-chain martingale proof and finite-horizon Doob proof against their SSEP consumers. The uses retain Choice, arbitrary finite rate matrices, the construction filtration, square integrability, continuous predictable compensators and càdlàg paths. Singleton sectors and T = 0 are handled.

The bridge lemma and equilibrium quasi-potential theorem use the Fourier heat-flow lemma with Countable Choice and matching torus normalization. Strict interior range preservation is obtained by affine rescaling; smooth endpoint behavior, long-time decay and connector matching are established in the downstream argument. The action definition and variational theorem expressly avoid asserting a microscopic path-space large-deviation principle.
